First and foremost, CCP isn't a game, and whoever has the highest CCP does not win. What I like to see is participation, not just lurking, so I was thinking of ways to encourage continual participation while also preventing some users from becoming "untouchable" (CCP so high they can't be downvoted into silence by the community). I was originally thinking that CCP needed a hard cap (positive and negative), but that still gives users/sock puppets the ability to get the initial 100 CCP required for downvoting, go silent, and just keep downvoting at will.

Then it dawned on me that CCP that expires solves all of those problems, and maybe even more. For one thing, acquiring as much CCP as possible no longer becomes a game (see former Redditor Unidan or GallowBoob) since the CCP will expire after a set time (eg, 3-6 months), and if said user stops posting altogether they will eventually return to 0 CCP. This should also work for negative CCP, though maybe it needs to be a longer time period.

Other benefits include:

  • Lurkers and sock puppets will be forced to comment periodically to retain their ability to downvote.
  • CCP circlejerkers will lose their "prize", and comments overall should improve site wide.
  • Accounts created for the sole purpose of selling for profit will lose their value and become worthless.

So yeah, I'd like to see an expiration date for CCP (maybe even SCP) of 3-6 months. What does Voat think?
